bidAggregate.note: Acknowledgement logs do not expose zero decisions that needed no network call. An acknowledgement timestamp is not a submission timestamp. Explicit Auction closed failures are real; nonlogged auctions cannot automatically be called deadline misses.

limitations: Seven completed matches, all Vickrey/second-price. No first-price live inference.
The window spans worker restarts and calibration changes; the log does not stamp full parameter snapshots per match. This is diagnosis, not a controlled version comparison.
Historical participant balances, rewards, paid prices and post-match winning-bid archives are public. No live spectator top bids or opponent hidden holdings were queried.

Unplayed tile COUNT is exact from starting5+awards−playedlength. Identities of unplayed tiles are not assumed. Own starting5 were nevertheless fully inferable in all seven cases from public time-ordered deficits.

Static repacking is a lexical diagnostic that ignores funding and timing. Short-word-only conditional repacking preserves observed bids/payments affordability, but rival policies may react to changed public score/balance, so it is not causal proof.
Sparse closed-auction failure logs do not expose every intentional zero decision or exact server submission time; missing logs cannot automatically be treated as deadline misses.
conclusions: Main observed loss is poor scoring/reinvestment efficiency: .419points per spentcoin vs winners .613; own4.07 meanwordlength vs5.43, with15 of28words being2point two-letter cashouts.
Winners buy17.43 tiles/match vs own12.14 at almost the same unit cost; their bigger payouts fund more acquisition. Simply reducing endcash does not explain the gap: own17.14 vs winners24.86.

Ordinary losing bid caps5–9 systematically trail actual archived winning bids13–17; too-cheap rebuilding occurs alongside occasional expensive rare letters cashed into rewards smaller than their purchase price.
Three explicit Auctionclosed failures among476auctionwindows and measured compute max240.5ms are real operational losses, but evidence does not support them as the dominant59.14point mean gap.
Holding only already-observed shortwordletters for regrouping adds19points total across7matches and flips no wins; a blunt ban on2letterwords is not a demonstrated solution.
